name: Irish Human Rights and Equality Commission
request_description: a copy of any briefing document of the nature described in the following in the June '24 board minutes: 1.2 Reflection on Thought Forum and Strategic Planning update Barry Price joined for this item. The Commission discussed the second event in the series of Thought Forums, which had taken place earlier in the day on the topic of ‘Artificial Intelligence and Digital Transformation’. The Commission agreed that it was an excellent session and noted it’s thanks to those who spoke at the event. The Commission noted that, as the National Human Rights Institution and National Equality Body, it may have a role to play in the new domestic oversight framework for AI to be established further to the EU AI Act and Council of Europe Framework Convention. The Commission will engage further with the Department of Enterprise, Trade and Employment about its role in this regard. The Commission agreed it would be useful to have a briefing document on AI for discussion at a future meeting, given the range of themes and issues to be considered in this evolving area. The document should include consideration of any implications that the new EU Standards for Equality Bodies may have in respect of these matters when they come into force. Barry Price left the meeting.

name: Irish Human Rights and Equality Commission
request_description: access to the records expanding Legal Aid in Ireland to labour disputes and worker rights. Additional Context received: 1) Irish Legal Aid Board says on their website: We can provide advice only and some assistance in relation to employment matters. However it is important to note that we cannot provide representation in relation to internal disciplinary or external workplace relations hearings. 2) 19 March 2025 Head of Legal, Michael o’Neil: "…appeal to the Labour Court and challenge the Workplace Relations Commission decision, it would not be appropriate for the Commission to grant assistance in a case where it could not represent [] for the whole appeal. Considering this, you may apply for legal advice and representation from the Legal Aid Board. 4) 7 July 2025 (file name on ohscr.org website CEDAW_C_IRL_CO_8_63688_E.docx 2 UN Committee on the Elimination of Discrimination against Women mentions legal aid in Ireland in their concluding observations on the eighth periodic report of Ireland: The Committee remains to be deeply concerned about systemic barriers for women to access justice 17 (a) Systemic barriers: restrictive civil legal aid.., 17 (b) Additional barriers: intersecting forms of discrimination, lack of accessibility measures and procedural accommodations, lack of culturally appropriate services; 17 (c) Gaps in ensuring women's access to legal representation in all relevant areas of law, including labour discrimination The Committee recommends to: 18 (c) Expand access to legal aid and legal representation for women in all areas of law where discrimination occurs, including labour disputes, welfare benefits and other civil matters, ensuring that financial barriers do not prevent women from accessing justice; 5) 21 July 2025 IHREC Director Ms. Deirdre Molony 's view " it is open to [] to apply for legal advice and representation from the Legal Aid Board [in employment matters]". Based on above public records and IHREC documentation, if the required records exist they have been created in July 2025.”
